newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia PM urges more investment as tensions ease.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia PM urges more investment as tensions ease.

text.p: Cambodia's co-premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh on Friday said political tensions were easing in the country and investors should not be deterred from putting money in Cambodia.
"The situation is getting much better, much better. And I advise all investors to come and to contribute to investment in Cambodia," Ranariddh told reporters.

Tensions between Ranariddh and co-premier Hun Sen, whose parties formed a shaky coalition government following U.N.-sponsored elections in 1993, have created jitters among foreign investors in recent weeks.
Analysts have said the problems between the two premiers could worsen as Cambodia approaches national elections, scheduled for 1998.

Most recently, Taiwanese investors decided to delay feasibility studies into a $70 million investment zone in the country until after the elections, the local Cambodia Daily newspaper reported on Friday.
It quoted the local representative of the investors in Cambodia, Tep Rithivit, as saying "Cambodia is like a...soap opera, and investors don't have time for soap operas."
Ranariddh denied knowledge of any Taiwanese concerns.
Ranariddh's and Hun Sen's political parties will oppose each other in the polls, and some investors have said feuding between the leaders has caused them to delay large projects until after 1998.

Last week, Ranariddh declared null and void three contracts signed by one of the country's largest investors, the Malaysian Ariston Sdn Bhd, because the agreements had been signed by a rival politician and did not, he said, follow legal procedures.
Ariston has said it remains committed to working in Cambodia with both sides of the government despite the setback.
